$comment: Content-addressed integrity lock for the external Codex review. The PRIMARY integrity proof is the content hashes below, not a commit SHA and not a git tag. A commit cannot contain its own SHA (self-reference), and remote tag push is rejected by repository permissions, so neither can be required for a fresh clone to verify.
canonicalization: Repo-relative paths, POSIX '/' separators, UTF-8 path encoding
Paths sorted by UTF-8 bytes, never by locale collation
File bytes hashed exactly as stored: no line-ending translation, no encoding conversion
No timestamps, permissions, ownership or other filesystem metadata
Per-file line '<sha256-hex>  <path>\n'; tree hash = sha256 of their UTF-8 concatenation
implementation: reports/codex-package/hash-manifest.mjs — one implementation called by both the bash and PowerShell runners, so cross-platform parity is structural rather than asserted.
source_baseline_commit_role: Provenance / history evidence only. The product freeze point. NOT the integrity gate.
source_baseline_content_hash_role: Artifact identity evidence. THIS is the product-source gate value.
source_paths_note: Review documentation is excluded from the product-source hash by construction.
excluded_files_reason: Self-reference guard: a manifest cannot contain its own hash, and BASELINE.json carries the manifest values.
review_package_tag_note: A local tag was created as an integrity mechanism, but remote tag push was rejected by repository permissions. The gate therefore never requires it: its absence is recorded, not failed. A fresh clone verifies with content hashes alone.
handoff_history_commit_note: Latest known documentation commit at manifest creation. Provenance evidence only; superseded by the commit that carries this manifest.
reason: Documentation-only handoff and evidence refresh commits after product freeze. Product source verified byte-identical to the freeze point.
